trust_decision.summary: The deserializer decides whether an untrusted, deserialized value can be passed to a native Promise resolve/reject. Resolve assimilates thenables, so a `then` callable built by a plugin or reference gets invoked. The fix rejects thenables before deferred.s/deferred.f in packages/seroval/src/core/context/deserializer.ts.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'fromJSON() Promise thenable assimilation'. deserializePromise is the obvious Promise-node handler that fromJSON reaches, and it resolves the deferred directly with the deserialized value.

fix_sites.entry_point: fromJSON (packages/seroval/src/core/tree/index.ts:120) / fromCrossJSON (packages/seroval/src/core/cross/index.ts:177): Promise node with s=1
fromJSON / fromCrossJSON: Promise node with s=0 (reject branch)
fromCrossJSON with shared options.refs: PromiseConstructor node then PromiseSuccess node (cross/streaming chunk route); also reachable via fromJSON
fromCrossJSON with shared options.refs: PromiseConstructor node then PromiseFailure node

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All four fix sites are in packages/seroval/src/core/context/deserializer.ts. The closest out-of-scope-looking route is the cross-call PromiseSuccess/PromiseFailure path at packages/seroval/src/core/context/deserializer.ts:632-662: its deferred is created in one fromCrossJSON call and stored in shared refs (packages/seroval/src/core/cross/index.ts:184), then resolved in a later call. It is still in the same file.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: AbortSignalPlugin calls `.then` itself instead of going through Promise assimilation. It lives in the opt-in seroval-plugins package rather than core fromJSON, and its stream-mode parser only ever emits a real Promise there. So a solver can argue 'not the Promise-resolution sink, and plugin payloads are trusted shapes'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Promises that resolve to ordinary objects must keep round-tripping, including objects with a non-callable `then` data key ('then' is deliberately not blocked) and objects that contain thenables deeper down. AbortSignal stream payloads whose controller is a real Promise node must keep aborting. Blocking the 'then' key, or rejecting every object-valued resolution, breaks these.

thenable value built as an Object node whose `then` is a plugin- or reference-produced callable, or reached through an IndexedValue back-reference; the check runs on the final deserialized value, so indirection is covered (fix.diff:120-123)

O7_producer.where: packages/seroval/src/core/context/deserializer.ts:595-617 (plugin.deserialize maps a node to an arbitrary value, e.g. a callable at packages/plugins/web/abort-signal.ts:52-54); packages/seroval/src/core/reference.ts:31-36 (registered references)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: AbortSignalPlugin.deserialize passes any deserialized `controller` node to PROMISE_TO_ABORT_SIGNAL, which calls `.then(abort, abort)` on it with no check that it is a real Promise. That is the same invocation of an attacker-shaped `then` (type confusion), and the published fix does not touch it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Separate opt-in plugins package; it is a direct method call rather than Promise assimilation; the report names fromJSON Promise handling only.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Different package (packages/plugins vs packages/seroval). The entry is at packages/plugins/web/abort-signal.ts:123-124, and the needed fix (require instanceof Promise) differs from isThennable.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Async-iterator stream listener resolving a pending deferred with the raw streamed value (or a stream-to-Promise helper resolving with the stream's return value) instead of wrapping it in {done, value}.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same file already resolves deferreds with stream data (constructors.ts:198,215). Unwrapping the return value into a Promise is a natural convenience that a maintainer could write.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A plugin that converts a deserialized Stream into a Promise (for example a Response.json()-style or last-value helper) by calling resolve(value) in its return listener.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The plugins already bridge Streams into web objects through stream.on listeners. A Promise-returning variant would sit in another package from the core check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: isThennable requires typeof 'object', so a callable thenable (a plugin- or reference-produced function carrying a `then` property) passes the check, while native resolve still assimilates it.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Plugins may return functions (abort-signal.ts:52-54) and references can be functions (reference.ts:10-14). A planted plugin or reference callable with a `then` property is a plausible how-type differential.

O9_family: CWE-843 type confusion: an untrusted deserialized value is treated as a Promise or plain value, and its thenable `then` is invoked by native Promise resolution or by a direct call
